post.summary: Send a test of a draft campaign
post.description:
**Required scopes (all):** `campaigns:manage` · `campaigns:read`

Requires campaigns:manage and campaigns:read because the test can use stored recipient samples. Sends one copy of a draft campaign's content to a seed recipient, through the same rendering, sending, and BanSafe checks as a launched campaign. The seed recipient must be a number connected to your team. A test is not a campaign recipient and is not counted in the campaign's statistics or webhooks. A team can send 20 tests an hour, and at most 5 an hour to one seed recipient.

get.description:
**Required scope:** `campaigns:read`

Returns recipients as CSV in queue order. Unfiltered exports page up to 1,000 recipients per request. Each page starts with a header row. When more recipients match, the `Polymorfa-Next-Cursor` response header carries the cursor for the next page; it is absent on the last page. Each page is read when it is requested, so a recipient appears once, with the outcome it had when its page was read. A filtered export is one atomic page of up to 1,000 recipients; larger filtered results return 409, so changing statuses cannot silently omit matches between pages. The export contains outcomes and `failureReason` codes only, never message content or template variables.

post.summary: Create an audience from a campaign
post.description:
Creates an audience from the recipients of a previous campaign that had one `outcome`, to send them a follow-up campaign. The members are a snapshot taken when the request runs: later receipts, reads or replies on the source campaign do not change the audience. Numbers on the team's opt-out list are left out and counted in `optedOutCount`; each member keeps the template variables it had on the source campaign. Outcomes: `delivered` (the device confirmed delivery), `not_delivered` (sent, with no delivery confirmation), `read`, `not_read` (sent and not read, including sends never delivered), `replied`, `not_replied` (sent and no reply was attributed), and `failed` (confirmed failed sends; sends whose outcome is uncertain, such as a timeout waiting for WhatsApp, are excluded). Read outcomes depend on the recipient's read receipts. `404` means the campaign is not in your team (or not in `projectId` when given); `409` means no recipient that is not opted out has the outcome, and nothing is created.

Requires a team API key with `campaigns:manage`. Project tokens are not accepted.

projectId.description: Optional. When given, the campaign must belong to this project.

To recreate a profile deleted in the last 30 days, send the `revision` the delete returned as `expectedRevision`; a put without it returns 409 with a message naming that revision. A consent assertion records the customer's statement; it does not clear an opt-out or authorize a send. This beta requires enrollment and release eligibility.

projectId.description: Required when using a team API key. Project tokens derive the project from the credential.

PlatformCampaignReplyFlowDefinition.description: An acyclic graph of 2 to 12 steps. The entry step waits for the first reply and sends nothing. See the reply flows guide for step and branch shapes.

send.description: `text` (`text`), `buttons` (`body`, up to 3 `buttons` with `id` and `text`), `list` (`body`, `buttonText`, up to 10 `rows`), or `flow_form` (`flowId`, `body`, `buttonText`, `screen`; Official numbers only).

flowKey.description: Groups the revisions of one reply flow.

replyFlowId.description: Reply flow revision to run after replies, or null to detach it.

projectId.description: Required when using a team API key. Project tokens derive the project from the credential.

CampaignRecipientFailureReason.description: Why the recipient was not sent, or why its last attempt did not succeed. Null when nothing went wrong. `opted_out`: the number is on the team's opt-out list. `cold_held`: the number never wrote to the sending number and the campaign holds cold sends. `campaign_cancelled`: the campaign was stopped before this recipient was sent. `invalid_recipient`: the number is not a valid WhatsApp address. `session_not_connected`: the sending number was not connected. `ack_timeout`: WhatsApp did not acknowledge the send in time. `blocked_by_safety`: a safety check refused the send before it was attempted; the recipient waits for the campaign to resume. `send_failed`: WhatsApp refused the send, or its outcome could not be confirmed. `missing_variable`: the campaign was launched with `skipMissingVariables` and the recipient had no value and no fallback for a variable. `other`: any other reason. New codes may be added.

uniqueOpens.description: Recipients who opened the link at least once.

totalOpens.description: Every recorded open, including repeat opens.

action.description: The held command. Approving it runs that command.

reasons.description: Why the command was held. `audience_threshold`: a launch would send to more recipients than the team's threshold. `agent_request`: an AI agent asked through the hosted MCP server.

recipientCount.description: Recipients the command would send to: the frozen audience after opt-outs for a launch, the queued recipients for a resume or new start time.

scheduledAt.description: Requested start in Unix milliseconds; null starts when approved. Null for a resume.

decidedBy.description: The owner or admin who approved or rejected it.

operationId.description: The launch operation an approval started.

recipientThreshold.description: Launches that would send to more recipients than this need a team owner or admin. Null turns approval off.

matchedCount.description: Recipients of the source campaign with the outcome, before opt-outs were left out.

optedOutCount.description: Matched recipients left out because the number is on the team's opt-out list.

teamId.description: The teamId returned by the settings read. Must match the authenticated team.

locale.description: Required when enabled. Never inferred from a phone number.
